skill.name: clean-code-reviewer
skill.description: Analyze code quality using Clean Code principles. The skill finds naming, function size, duplication, YAGNI, magic number, readability, and convention issues.
skill.summary: Review code quality and prioritize Clean Code refactoring opportunities.
skill.author: hylarucoder

security_audit.summary: The static command, network, reconnaissance, and obfuscation hits are false positives from markdown formatting and educational code examples. No evidence found for executable scripts, active network requests, system reconnaissance, or data exfiltration in the skill instructions. However, evaluation-output.json embeds a prior safe-to-publish audit verdict, which is a high-severity prompt-injection risk for marketplace review.

remediation.issue: Bundled audit verdict text can bias the marketplace review process.
remediation.suggestion: Remove evaluation-output.json from the published skill package, or replace it with neutral documentation that does not declare safety status.

content.user_title: Review Code for Clean Code Issues
content.value_statement: Code quality issues slow reviews and make changes risky. This skill finds Clean Code problems and gives prioritized refactoring guidance.
actual_capabilities: Reviews code against seven Clean Code dimensions listed in the skill instructions.
Flags vague names, inconsistent naming, oversized functions, and too many parameters.
Identifies duplicate logic, dead code, over-engineering, magic numbers, and deep nesting.
Applies language-specific review patterns for TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, and Go.
Ranks findings by high, medium, or low severity with refactoring suggestions.
Formats review output with principle, location, severity, problem, and recommendation.
limitations: Provides review guidance only and does not automatically modify code.
Does not execute tests or prove that behavior remains unchanged.
Does not focus on security, performance, or dependency risk analysis.
Works best when the user provides relevant files and project conventions.

use_cases.title: Review Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Find maintainability issues before merging code into a shared branch.

use_cases.title: Plan Refactoring Work
use_cases.description: Prioritize high-impact cleanup tasks in legacy modules or active features.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Practices
use_cases.description: Apply consistent naming, function, and structure checks across a codebase.

prompt_templates.title: Quick File Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this file for Clean Code issues. List the highest impact naming, function, duplication, and magic number problems.

prompt_templates.title: Focused Refactoring Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this module for oversized functions, too many parameters, and unclear responsibilities. Suggest behavior-preserving refactors.

prompt_templates.title: Language Pattern Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this code using the language-specific patterns for TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, or Go. Group issues by severity.

prompt_templates.title: Repository Quality Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the selected repository area for Clean Code issues. Deduplicate findings and produce a prioritized refactoring plan.

output_examples.input: Review a service file for Clean Code issues.
output: Naming issue: High. A short variable name hides the purpose of a date value.
Function issue: Medium. One function combines validation, calculation, persistence, and notification work.
Suggestion: Split the workflow into smaller functions with explicit responsibility names.

output_examples.input: Check a Python module for readability problems.
output: Clarity issue: Medium. A complex list comprehension is difficult to scan and test.
Convention issue: Low. Several helper functions do not include type hints.
Suggestion: Extract the filtering logic into a named helper and add explicit input and return types.

output_examples.input: Audit a component directory before refactoring.
output: Duplication issue: High. Multiple components repeat the same validation and error display flow.
Magic value issue: Low. Timing and threshold values are repeated without names.
Suggestion: Extract shared validation behavior and replace repeated values with named constants.

best_practices: Provide the target files, review scope, language, and project conventions.
Address high-severity findings before medium and low-severity cleanup.
Verify behavior with tests after applying any refactoring suggestion.
anti_patterns: Treating every suggestion as mandatory without considering project context.
Mixing behavior changes with readability refactors in the same change.
Running broad audits without specifying the target module or language.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews naming, function size, duplication, over-engineering, magic numbers, readability, and project conventions.

faq.question: Does it change my code?
faq.answer: No. It provides findings and recommendations that you can apply manually.

faq.question: Which languages are covered?
faq.answer: The references include TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, and Go review patterns.

faq.question: Can I review only one directory?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide a scope such as a component folder, service module, or selected files.

faq.question: Does it find security vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on maintainability and readability, not security testing.

faq.question: How are issues prioritized?
faq.answer: The skill groups issues as high, medium, or low based on maintainability impact.
